thread:
jordan: FYI a customer opened a ticket — their Node/TS SDK v0.23.1 is 404'ing when calling chat.create but curl to the API succeeds. Repro attached.

maria: Can you paste the minimal repro here?

jordan: Paste below (sanitized keys):
```
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-7b', prompt: 'hi' });
```
Response is a 404 with body: `{ "error": "route_not_found", "message": "chat.create not found" }`

alex: Interesting — our API uses `chat.create` historically but recent server rollout accepted `chat.completions` as canonical. Did the SDK migrate route names? :thinking: @maria any idea?

maria: I think v0.23 introduced a route rename mapping but only for the hosted control plane. If the customer's account pinned an older model variant or private deployment, the shim may not be applied. Are they on Private or Dedicated?

jordan: Ticket says "Dedicated (reserved)" in us-west, account id: acct_XX. They reported that `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.create` returns 200 and expected JSON. The SDK does internal RPC to our control plane, different path.

ingrid: We should check request ids. Jordan can you grab the request id from the SDK logs and the curl call so we can correlate?

jordan: From SDK log: `req=01GZK... runtime-route=chat.create status=404 x-request-id=ri_9a7b`
Curl returned: `x-request-id: ri_9a9d`

alex: Different request ids => calls hit different frontends. Looks like the sdk goes to the control-plane router which expects the new canonical names. The customer's dedicated endpoint still exposes legacy route mapping. So the SDK's new canonical name doesn't exist on their private/dedicated router.

maria: Short-term mitigation: advise customer to pin SDK to v0.22.x (which used legacy route names) OR call the endpoint directly with raw HTTP using `chat.create` path. Example curl shim: `POST https://dedicated.us-west.redwood.ai/v1/chat.create` with same auth header.

jordan: Customer asked for a patch so they don't have to downgrade. Any quick client-side workaround?

alex: We can push a tiny patch to the SDK that tries the original route name on 404s for dedicated/private accounts: fallback logic — attempt `chat.create` then if 404 try `chat.completions`. But we need eng-runtime signoff because it masks server inconsistencies. @deploy-bot can we get a canary build pipeline run for this patch?

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline queued for branch sdk-route-fallback. CI will run unit tests and a small e2e against a staging dedicated router.

maria: Also check param name changes — the SDK currently sends `prompt` field but newer API expects `input` in the canonical route. If the dedicated router expects `prompt` but the canonical route uses `input`, that could cause parse errors (different symptom). Jordan, does the 404 body include any parameter hints?

jordan: 404 only says route not found. However customer also reported a later 400 when they retried with a v0.23 patched client: `400 bad_request: unknown field 'prompt'` — so yes, param name mismatch exists when they hit the canonical route.

ingrid: Ok so two issues: route name mismatch (chat.create vs chat.completions) and param renames (prompt -> input). This happens because their dedicated deployment hasn't been upgraded to accept the canonical names.

alex: Action items: Jordan to share account id and logs with eng-runtime (done). Maria to draft the mitigation note to the customer: 1) temporary pin to SDK v0.22.x OR use raw HTTP to the dedicated endpoint with legacy route/params; 2) we can run a compatibility shim on their router if they want, but that requires operations approval; 3) we will open an internal ticket to add a graceful fallback in the SDK if safe.

jordan: I'll send the mitigation message and ask if they want us to schedule a compatibility rollout. Also I'll include repro steps for eng:
```
# repro
export REDWOOD_KEY=sk_live_xxx
node -e "const _ = require('@redwood/inference'); const c=new _.default({apiKey:process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}); c.chat.create({model:'redwood-7b',prompt:'hi'}).catch(e=>console.error(e));"
# observe 404 and x-request-id header
```

maria: For the internal ticket, include the dedicated router version (they're on 2025-01-15 build) and note the param and route name deltas. Tag with priority P2 since customer has a downgrade available.

alex: Also add a note about monitoring: set an alert for `sdk_route_mismatch` on error spikes across dedicated accounts so we can catch regressions sooner.

jordan: Customer accepted the temp pin to v0.22 and asked for ETA on a non-downgrade fix. I'll escalate to eng-runtime and keep them posted. :thumbsup:

ingrid: Thanks team — please update the ticket with the canary results when deploy-bot finishes.

deploy-bot: CI passed for sdk-route-fallback branch; canary scheduled for staging-dedicated-router at 2165441200.
